standard_prerequisites.name: Product precategory
standard_prerequisites.statement: The product of two precategories has pairs of objects as objects and pairs of morphisms as morphisms, with the componentwise structure.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the domain of the functors on the left hand side.

standard_prerequisites.name: Functor precategory
standard_prerequisites.statement: For precategories B and C the functor precategory has functors as objects and natural transformations as morphisms.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the codomain on the right hand side.

standard_prerequisites.name: Natural transformation and functoriality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A natural transformation is a family of morphisms commuting with the action on morphisms, and a functor must respect composition and identities.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are what the two constructions have to produce.

core_obligations: From a functor F out of the product build, for each object a, the functor F_a on B, giving a function on objects of A (source lines 907-909).

On a morphism f of A use the components of F at the pairs (a,b) and (a prime,b) to build a natural transformation from F_a to F_a prime, whose functoriality in a yields the functor from A to the functor precategory (source lines 909-913).

Conversely, from a functor G into the functor precategory define the action on objects of the product and, for a pair of morphisms, the morphism obtained by composing the two induced morphisms, noting that the two ways of composing agree by naturality (source lines 915-921).

Check that these two operations are inverse to each other (source line 922, where the author states that this is clear, together with the functoriality checks deferred in the two preceding paragraphs, both retained verbatim in the editorial note).

proof_roadmap.step: From a functor on the product to a functor into the functor precategory.
Conversely, from a functor into the functor precategory to one on the product.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 899-905 (book Lemma 9.5.3): for precategories A, B, C the type of functors from the product of A and B to C is equivalent to the type of functors from A to the functor precategory of B and C. The statement gives the two types and nothing else, and the proof (source lines 906-923) has to build both directions: on the one hand it must produce, from a functor on the product, its fibres at each object of A together with the natural transformations induced by the morphisms of A; on the other hand it must define the action on pairs of morphisms and notice that the two candidate composites agree by naturality of the given functor; and finally it must observe that the two constructions are inverse. The author explicitly defers the functoriality checks and the inverse verification as easy or clear, which this card records verbatim, so what is counted is the pair of constructions and the naturality observation, not those routine verifications.
